root_cause.text: In `amdgpu_device_gpu_recover()` the code dereferenced `job->pasid` after `drm_sched_start()` could let the TDR workqueue free the `struct amdgpu_job`, creating a use-after-free race between the sched timeout callback and job teardown.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `int pasid = job ? job->pasid : -EINVAL;` at the start of `amdgpu_device_gpu_recover()` and later replaces `job->pasid` access with the cached `pasid`, with comments explicitly stating “the job may be freed before the end of the reset” and “The job may already be freed at this point via the sched tdr workqueue,” while the CVE description says the timeout callback and TDR queue race can free the job before `pasid` is accessed, causing a UAF.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In `amdgpu_device_gpu_recover()` the code dereferenced `job->pasid` after `drm_sched_start()` could let the TDR workqueue free the `struct amdgpu_job`, creating a use-after-free race between the sched timeout callback and job teardown.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `int pasid = job ? job->pasid : -EINVAL;` at the start of `amdgpu_device_gpu_recover()` and later replaces `job->pasid` access with the cached `pasid`, with comments explicitly stating “the job may be freed before the end of the reset” and “The job may already be freed at this point via the sched tdr workqueue,” while the CVE description says the timeout callback and TDR queue race can free the job before `pasid` is accessed, causing a UAF.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cache the job PASID early in GPU recovery so it remains available after the job may be freed during reset handling.
intent_record.what: A new local integer variable named `pasid` is added near the start of `amdgpu_device_gpu_recover()`, initialized from `job->pasid` when `job` is non-NULL, or to `-EINVAL` otherwise, with an accompanying comment explaining that the PASID is saved early because the job may be freed before reset completes.
intent_record.how: This preserves the PASID value for later use during GPU recovery/reset even if the original job object is released before the recovery path finishes, preventing use-after-free or loss of context during error handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix GPU recovery to avoid using a freed job pointer by switching to the cached PASID for task info lookup.
intent_record.what: In amdgpu_device_gpu_recover(), the code no longer reads job->pasid directly when building task info for the wedged event. Instead, it adds a comment explaining the job may already be freed by sched TDR workqueue, and it uses the cached pasid variable to call amdgpu_vm_get_task_info_pasid() only when pasid is non-negative.
intent_record.how: This avoids dereferencing a potentially freed job pointer during GPU recovery, preventing a use-after-free risk and ensuring task info can still be looked up safely from the cached PASID when available.

grouping_result.intent: Fix GPU recovery to avoid using a freed job pointer by switching to the cached PASID for task info lookup.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix GPU recovery by caching and reusing the job PASID so task info lookup does not depend on a potentially freed job pointer during reset handling.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly address the reported use-after-free in amdgpu_device_gpu_recover() by avoiding dereference of job->pasid after drm_sched_start() may allow the job to be freed. Caching the PASID and using it for task info lookup matches the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This dereferences job->pasid after recovery/reset handling can race with job teardown and free the struct amdgpu_job, creating the use-after-free described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement dereferences job->pasid during GPU recovery. Per the root cause, drm_sched_start() can allow the TDR workqueue to free struct amdgpu_job, so accessing job here creates a use-after-free race between recovery and job teardown.

Author: André Almeida <andrealmeid@igalia.com>
Date:   Tue Jun 17 09:49:49 2025 -0300

    drm/amdgpu: Make use of drm_wedge_task_info
    
    To notify userspace about which task (if any) made the device get in a
    wedge state, make use of drm_wedge_task_info parameter, filling it with
    the task PID and name.
    
    Reviewed-by: Christian König <christian.koenig@amd.com>
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20250617124949.2151549-7-andrealm
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown code no longer dereferences job->pasid directly after any scheduling or teardown boundary in a way that indicates the reported UAF. Instead, it uses the PASID only to look up task info: `if (job) ti = amdgpu_vm_get_task_info_pasid(adev, job->pasid);` and then passes `ti ? &ti->task : NULL` to `drm_dev_wedged_event()`. The added `amdgpu_vm_put_task_info(ti);` also shows the lookup result is reference-managed. Because the root cause was a dereference of `job->pasid` leading to use-after-free, and this snippet replaces that with task-info lookup and cleanup, the fix is already present in this commit. The vulnerable construct itself is not present here.
